summary: Siskiyou County fire lookout northeast of Etna; 1931 plans for a lookout house; NHLR-registered 2016; 2019 fire nearby; road behind locked gates on private land.

facts.agency: California Department of Forestry & Fire Protection (CAL FIRE)

access.note: Road to the tower crosses private property with locked gates; April 2020 blog says visitors are not welcome. No official visitor information found.

visit.trail_note: Road to the tower crosses private property behind locked gates, per an April 2020 blog post. Ask CAL FIRE Siskiyou unit before any visit.

events.note: Feb 23, 1931 newspaper: fire telephone line from Etna to the rock (twelve miles) and planned lookout station; Apr 4, 1931 newspaper: standard lookout house to be erected on Duzel Rock. Completion date not found.
Division of Forestry photographer Vern F. Knedler photographed the lookout looking northeast on July 16, 1953 (Black Cards collection)

Duzel Fire started 09/07/2019 6:19 PM near Duzel Rock Lookout, northeast of Etna; 15 acres; contained 09/10/2019 7:27 PM; cause under investigation. The CAL FIRE page does not mention the lookout's condition.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: A February 1931 newspaper item spells the rock Duzzle Rock; the April 1931 item, the Register, CAL FIRE and the archive record use Duzel Rock. The record keeps Duzel.

notes_for_editor: Brief's record (elevation 1841.3 m, agency, NHLR US 1152 registration on Nov 27, 2016) matches the Register; no corrections. Brief had no build event; the sources show 1931 plans only, so no built event is asserted. The 1953 Knedler photograph (archive.org/details/casbcfm_000249, public domain per the archive record) is a new find but its image file URL was not fetched, so no photos entry is included; the editor can pull the JPG from that item. The April 2020 blog is a personal account; only the access fact was used and the author is not named. Staffing and current condition beyond the 2020 blog and 2019 fire are not in the sources read. The fire page shows no damage to the lookout.
